full_judgment:
(I) Whether, in the facts and the circumstances of the case, the tribunal judicious in upholding the order of the AACT who confirmed DCT's dis-allowances of the provision of leave pay and gratuity on actual basis inasmuch as, to the fact that it is an expenditure incurred for the year and for the purpose of business which is allowable under section 29(1 )(XXVII) of IT Ordinance, 1984 subject to limitation set out in section 30(e) ? 

 (II) Whether, in the facts and on the circumstances of the case, the tribunal is judicious in disallowing, office entertainment expenses which is allowable under section 29(l)(XXVI- II) read with limitation set out in Rule 65 of the IT Rules, 1984 once ordered to allow later? 

 8. Mr. Abdur Rahim Bhuiyan, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing with Ms .Kazi Zinnat Hoq, also invites our attention to sections 29(1)(XXVII) and 30(e) of the Ordinance and contends that the provision of leave pay and gratuity of the employees may be made on the provision of perquisites subject to the limitation of section 30(e) of the Ordinance. He, however, contends that as it is not possible to decide the facts about the actual entitlement of the assessee considering its actual number of employees, this question cannot be decided in reference application and it should be sent back on remand to the Tribunal to assess the actual entitlement of the assessee on the provision of perquisites. 

 16. Considering the reference application, supplementary affidavit, affidavit-in-reply and the submissions of the learned Advocate as well as the learned Assistant Attorney General for the respective parties and having regard to the relevant provisions of sections 29(1)(XXVIl), 30(e) of the Ordinance we are of the view that an assessee is entitled to get allowance on leave pay and gratuity subject to the limitation under section 30(e) as "leave pay and gratuity are "benefit to an employee" for which provision of perquisites are allowable expenditure. However, the Tribunal allowed partial expenditure on this head and in deciding a reference application it is not permissible to assess the entitlement of the assessee considering the number of employees. Therefore; the Tribunal must consider the number of employees and the provision of section 30(e) of the Ordinances and decide this question in the light of our observation.
